items.content: If you really want to hear about it, the first thing you'll probably want to know is where I was born, and what my lousy childhood was like, and how my parents were occupied and all before they had me, and all that David Copperfield kind of crap, but I don't feel like going into it, if you want to know the truth.
items.explanation: Holden Caulfield's famous opening monologue, 1951. The anti-literary pose — refusing to do what a novel usually does — is a human adolescent voice that AI tends to flatten.
items.source: J.D. Salinger — The Catcher in the Rye (1951)

items.content: She had not expected it. Pulling back the curtain in the grey half-light of early morning, she found the world had been quietly remade while she slept — the garden smoothed to a clean, featureless white, the familiar oak reduced to a dark sketch of itself against the pale sky. Everything was muffled, held, as though the night had pressed a finger to its lips. She stood there a long moment, her breath fogging the cold glass, reluctant to look away.

items.content: The fog had swallowed the city whole by half past five, leaving only the nearest lamppost visible, its orange halo dissolving into grey gauze a few feet beyond. She walked without destination, her footsteps swallowed by the damp air, the familiar streets made strange and provisional, as though the city were still deciding what shape it wanted to take. A bus shelter emerged from the murk, then retreated behind her. Somewhere nearby, water dripped from an unseen ledge in steady, indifferent rhythm.

items.content: The train lurches forward with a groan, pressing strangers together in a reluctant intimacy. Shoulders touch, breath mingles, and eyes study the middle distance with practiced vacancy, each person building invisible walls against the crush. Somewhere beneath the screech of metal on metal, a phone leaks tinny music, someone's coffee breathes warmth into the stale air. At each station the doors exhale bodies and swallow new ones, the city feeding itself into the dark tunnels like a slow, indifferent pulse.
